exact_statement: For every finite increasing weighted threshold f=2*1{sum w_j X_j>=t}-1 with arbitrary positive real weights and independent interior Bernoulli(q_j) inputs, every i with pivotal probability rho_i>0, and every integer r>=1, let d_i be the pivotal interval indicator, nu_i(B)=dhat_i(B)^2/rho_i in the orthonormal product Fourier basis, U_i,r={j!=i:w_j>=w_i/r}, L_i,r=2 sum_{j in U_i,r} min(q_j,1-q_j), and K_i,r(B)=|B intersect U_i,r|. For 0<epsilon<=1, E_nu_i (1-epsilon)^K_i,r <= min(1,r/sqrt(epsilon L_i,r)). With r_k=2^k and pi_k=1/[(k+1)(k+2)], put R_i(B)=sup_{k>=0} pi_k^2 L_i,r_k/[4^k(K_i,r_k(B)+1)]. Then Pr_nu_i(ln^+ R_i>u)<=min(1,sqrt(2e)*exp(-u/2)) for u>=0, E_nu_i ln^+ R_i<=3+ln 2, and sum_i sum_{S containing i} fhat_mu(S)^2 ln^+ R_i(S without i)<=(3+ln 2) I_mu(f). A zero L gives score zero and noise upper bound one. Signed weights are oriented and zero weights/deterministic inputs contracted. This is a rank payment in natural units, not a corrected FEI+ theorem.
hypotheses: arbitrary finite arity and real threshold
independent product input law; endpoints contracted
natural logarithms; scale prior fixed before sampling

exact_statement: Let X~Ber(p), Y~Ber(1/4) be independent and f=1-2XY. For the physical reveal A={X}, let M=H(S_X|S_Y) under the squared orthonormal product Fourier law and J=H(S_Y)-E_X H(spectrum(f_X)), in bits. Then lim_{p downarrow 0}(J-M)/[p log_2(1/p)]=1/2. Therefore every scalar tau(p) making J<=M+tau(p) valid for all Boolean functions, all product measures, and one-bit physical reveals satisfies liminf_{p downarrow 0} tau(p)/[p log_2(1/p)]>=1/2; no fixed finite O(p) correction is sufficient. No optimality of coefficient one or composition payment is asserted.
refutes: Universal scalar one-bit uncertainty correction tau(p)<=K*p for fixed finite K
